notes: Synthetic callers only: every name, address, phone number (555) and email (example.com) here is invented. No customer data.

Each scenario fixes the world around the live conversation loop: caller identity/context, office hours, tool results (arrays step per call, the last entry repeats; { hang: true } never settles so the relay's own time bound fires; capture/booking/reservice/transfer flags perform the same ctx side effects the real tools do).

expect = deterministic checks with a severity (critical | major | quality) and optional adjudicated flag; spec = what the judge grades against. Adam adjudicates majors per scenario after a first run by setting adjudicated: true — never by pinning outputs.
Regexes are case-insensitive JavaScript sources. Tool names must be registered tools.

Dates in booking fixtures are run-relative tokens ({{day+N}} → "Wednesday September 16", {{dow+N}}, {{monthday+N}}, {{iso+N}}), rendered once per run from the ET date the run started on, so "next week" stays next week on every weekly run.

Every scenario answers every tool its gates register (a generic "not on file" / "not available" answer where the scenario has nothing specific): the harness treats a tool call the fixture does not answer as a replay error, because the world was no longer fixed.

allowedTools is the scenario's explicit allowlist, separate from which tools the fixture answers: every call outside it — a stray write above all — is a blocking critical miss (allowed_tools), and a call the fixture REJECTED for its arguments never counts as the tool being called.

A toolResponses entry may carry `when` (argument matchers — the answer belongs to those arguments; a schema-valid but scenario-wrong call gets a refusal instead) and `once` (consumed by its first match). Conditioned entries are tried first; unconditioned ones step by call count.
